Decisions.title: Decision workbench
Decisions.description: Freeze the candidates and their vitals, then come back in 30/90 days to see whether the call was right.

steps.createBody: One board per call — "picking a vector database", say.
steps.addBody: Each one is frozen with its vitals as they are the moment you add it.
steps.decideBody: A sentence on why; come back in 30/90 days and compare.

Decisions.emptyDescription: A board records one decision: the candidates, what they looked like at the time, and why you landed where you did.
Decisions.createDialogDescription: Start by saying what you are deciding. A board holds one decision, so "vector database" beats "tech choices".
Decisions.createTitleHint: One sentence: what this board is deciding.
Decisions.createSummaryPlaceholder: Search for an internal service; we are on Postgres at around 10M rows
Decisions.createSummaryHint: The constraints you had. This is what the person reading it in three months uses to recall why the choice was limited.
Decisions.editDescription: Title and context. Candidates and verdicts are not edited here — they are the parts of this record that need to keep their history.
Decisions.notFoundDescription: It was deleted, or this link points at somebody else's board.
Decisions.candidatesDescription: Put them side by side. A verdict is what you called each one while comparing, and you can change it later.
Decisions.frozenHint: These numbers are each candidate's vitals at the moment you added it, and they do not change afterwards. For what a repository looks like today, open its project page.
Decisions.emptyBoardDescription: Search for a repository below — adding it freezes its vitals as they are now into this record.
Decisions.addHint: Search by repository name. Adding it freezes its vitals as they are now.
Decisions.removeDescription: Its note and its frozen vitals go with it. Copy anything you want to keep first.
Decisions.notePlaceholder: What is wrong with this one
Decisions.full: A board holds at most {max}. Remove one before adding another.
Decisions.outcomeDescription: Which one you took and why. This is the part the 30/90-day check comes back to read.
Decisions.outcomeReplaceHint: Rewriting overwrites the text and the date. Changing your mind is fine, but the earlier call is then gone.
Decisions.outcomePlaceholder: Why this one, or why none of them
Decisions.noOutcome: No outcome yet. Waiting until the candidates are all in is fine.
Decisions.allAdded: Every repository that matched is already a candidate on this board. Search for another.
Decisions.duplicateCandidate: That repository is already a candidate on this board.

ApiKeys.title: API Keys
ApiKeys.description: Keys for calling the Open Radar API on your own behalf. A key can read rankings and submit repositories; publishing projects stays an operator action.
ApiKeys.name: Name
ApiKeys.empty: You have no API keys yet.
ApiKeys.emptyHint: Create one to call the API from a script or a scheduled job. The plaintext is shown once — store it before you close this dialog.
ApiKeys.revokeConfirm: Revoke this key? Anything still using it will start getting 401s immediately.
ApiKeys.rotateConfirm: Rotate this key? The current key stops working immediately and its plaintext cannot be recovered.
ApiKeys.secretWarning: This is the only time the key will be shown. We store only a hash, so it cannot be displayed again — if you lose it, rotate.
ApiKeys.rotateDone: Rotated. The new key is shown below; the old one no longer works.
ApiKeys.quotaHint: The limit is {limit}. Revoke the ones you no longer use, or give up ownership of one to let an operator manage it.
ApiKeys.rotateStale: This key has not been rotated in a while. Rotating changes nothing about its permissions.
ApiKeys.auditDescription: Who changed which key, and when. The key list only shows current state — this is the history.
ApiKeys.tierHint: User keys have an owner and can be managed by them. Service keys belong to nobody and only an operator can manage them.
ApiKeys.ownerHint: An owned key can also be revoked by its owner in /console. Leave empty for a service integration key.
ApiKeys.issuedOnBehalf: Issuing on behalf of an account
ApiKeys.reasonHint: Recorded in the audit log. Required — it is the only thing that explains this change later.
ApiKeys.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. key leaked in a public gist
ApiKeys.revokeDone: Revoked. Anything using it gets 401s immediately.
ApiKeys.rotateDoneAdmin: Rotated. Hand the new plaintext over out of band.
ApiKeys.noChange: Nothing changed, so nothing was recorded.
ApiKeys.secretStored: I have stored this key somewhere safe

Subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
Subscriptions.description: Have this radar push repository data to a callback URL you control. The verification key is derived from the api key you pick, so every subscription on that key shares one.
Subscriptions.adminDescription: Every subscription, both console accounts and API keys. Read-only except for disabling: a subscriber's filters and callback URL are theirs to change.
Subscriptions.formDescription: Everything after creation is driven by the callback URL and the filters below; the verification key comes from the api key you pick.
Subscriptions.name: Name
Subscriptions.callbackUrlHint: Where payloads are POSTed. Each request carries an X-Webhook-Signature header you verify with the signing key.
Subscriptions.scopesHint: At least one. These define what the subscription pushes to your endpoint.
Subscriptions.filterRepoIdsHint: One per line (commas work too). Filling this in overrides every filter below it.
Subscriptions.emptyHint: Create one to have repository data pushed to your own endpoint. The verification key is derived from the api key you pick — the verification guide has the recipe.
Subscriptions.noDeliveries: No delivery has been attempted yet.
Subscriptions.sendTestConfirm: POST one small test payload to this callback now? It does not move the delivery watermark.
Subscriptions.editDescription: Changing the filters rewinds the watermark to the earliest stored period of the newly matched set, so newly included repositories are delivered at least once.
Subscriptions.editFiltersHint: Saving rewinds the watermark and bumps the filter version, which is how a subscriber tells new data from a re-send.
Subscriptions.removeConfirm: Delete this subscription? Its delivery queue goes with it and nothing further will be sent.
Subscriptions.disableConfirm: Disable this subscription? The subscriber can re-enable it themselves, and delivery stops after the current attempt finishes.
Subscriptions.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. callback pointed at an unrelated host
Subscriptions.createdBody: The radar will push to your callback URL on the cadence you picked, starting from the next run that has new data.
Subscriptions.createdVerify: There is no second secret to keep: the verification key is derived from the api key this subscription signs with, so you compute it yourself. The recipe, a ready-to-run verifier and every reason a check fails are in the guide.
Subscriptions.createdDocsLink: How to verify a delivery signature
Subscriptions.signingKeyHint: That key doubles as the signing key: the verification key is derived from its key_hash, so all subscriptions on it share one. Switching keys changes the verification key — the receiver must update.
Subscriptions.signingKeyEmpty: No usable api key yet. Issue one under "API Keys" first, then come back.
Subscriptions.paidGateDescription: Creating a repository subscription is a Pro feature. Only paid accounts can create one.
Subscriptions.paidRequiredError: Creating a subscription needs Pro. Open it and come back.

Billing.title: Billing
Billing.description: Payments and entitlements from the radar's own checkout. Read-only: a console never rewrites a row of money, only the settlement program does.
Billing.mySubscriptionDescription: Your Pro plan and when it runs out. Renewing while it is active is 20% off.
Billing.renewNote: Renewals are 20% off and tack onto the current expiry — early renewal never overwrites time you already paid for.
Billing.notSubscribedDescription: Pro unlocks push subscriptions and monitoring alerts. Open it here and pay by scanning WeChat Pay.
Billing.historyDescription: Every checkout order you placed, whatever it became. Amounts are shown in yuan; a renewal keeps the discounted price it was paid at.
Billing.subscriptionsDescription: Accounts holding an open entitlement. Expiry is the whole of the state — a row whose activeUntil is past is a former subscriber.
Billing.ordersDescription: Every checkout order, whatever it became. Amounts are stored in fen and shown in yuan; a rejected callback stays rejected.
Billing.searchPlaceholder: Search name, email or order id
